## Linear Algebra: Theory and Applications

This is the course website for **MATH 332 — Fall 2026 Section 002** at Illinois
Institute of Technology.

## Course Description

This course develops the theory and applications of linear algebra through
systems of equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and
eigenvectors, and inner product spaces. Python will support visualization,
numerical computation, symbolic computation, and experimentation.

{{< include classlib/classlib/quarto/snippets/fred-hickernell-bio.qmd >}}

## Required course materials

- **WileyPLUS access:** WileyPLUS is required for this course. All homework
  will be assigned, completed individually, and automatically graded through
  WileyPLUS. Launch each homework assignment from
  [Canvas]({{< meta canvas.course >}}).
- **Textbook:** Howard Anton, *Elementary Linear Algebra: Applications
  Version*, 12th edition. Single-term WileyPLUS access includes the online
  textbook for the duration of the course, so a separate printed copy is
  optional. See [Resources](pages/resources.qmd) for details.

<details>
<summary><strong>Prerequisites</strong></summary>

The prerequisite is MATH 251. It will help to be familiar with:

- A bit of vectors and matrices (but not required)
- Jupyter notebooks

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Where to find it</strong></summary>

Class meetings combine whiteboard explanation with linked lecture slides,
live polls, and computational activities. Use the course website as the
starting point for each meeting, and come prepared to open the slides, Canvas,
and Jupyter notebooks during class.

The course website is the authoritative source for course information,
schedules, lecture notes, and assignment details. Use Canvas for announcements,
launching WileyPLUS homework, completing the diagnostic survey, and checking
grades.

## Assessment

- [**Homework assignments:**](pages/assignments.qmd) 20%; all homework
  assignments are completed individually through WileyPLUS
- [**Quizzes: 15%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); Quiz 1 is September 10;
  later dates **TBD**
- [**Tests: 25%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); Test 1 is not yet scheduled
- [**Final Exam: 40%**](pages/quizzes-and-tests.qmd); _on the date assigned by
  the registrar_
- **Extra Credit:** From August 24 through December 6, you may earn extra
  credit by being the first student to report a previously unreported error in

  - my lecture slides, Jupyter notebooks, or assignments at least 24 hours
    after the material was presented or posted; or
  - the textbook.

  Report each error by creating an [issue](https://github.com/fjhickernell/MATH332Fall2026/issues)
  in the course repository. Each confirmed error earns 0.5 or 1 percentage
  point, depending on the severity of the error, up to 10 percentage points
  total.

  Extra credit is added to your final weighted course total. *Canvas may not
  display the weighted total correctly until grades have been recorded in
  every assessment category.*
